sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: On-Site Factory Pre-Shipment Quality Control and Audit Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) between the Taiwan Strait sides (2010)
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised June 30, 2024, effective November 1, 2024); Beneficial Owner Information Management Measures of the People's Republic of China (Order No. 3 of the People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation, effective November 1, 2024); Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (Order No. 746); Measures on Customer Due Diligence and Retention of Customer Identity and Transaction Records (People's Bank of China Document No. 8 [2022]).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder (Company Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path for Taiwan-origin documents (since Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention state): (i) notarization by the Taiwan District Court; (ii) authentication by the Taiwan Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (iii) verification by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) in Taipei; (iv) confirmation by the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) and the provincial notary association in mainland China.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Business Registration Credentials) of the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same consular legalization path: Taiwan district court notarization, MOFA authentication, SEF verification, ARATS confirmation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the WFOE and appointment of its Legal Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the Board Resolution by a Taiwan district court notary, followed by SEF verification and ARATS confirmation; no Apostille because Taiwan is not a Hague member.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles of Incorporation) of the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The consolidated Articles must be notarized in Taiwan, verified by SEF, and confirmed by ARATS; a certified Chinese translation accompanies the instrument. Consular legalization does not apply due to absence of consular posts; the cross-strait verification serves as the authentication equivalent.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder (account conduct and credit standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank in Taiwan (signature by the relationship manager or branch manager)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter must be notarized by a Taiwan notary, then the bank's signature is authenticated, processed through SEF/ARATS, and a Chinese translation certified. No Apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, all UBOs and ultimate beneficial owners of the Taiwan corporate shareholder shall be screened against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, as supplemented by FDI and sectoral orders; (iii) the U.K. HM Treasury Consolidated List; (iv) the consolidated EU restrictive measures list; and (v) the relevant mainland Chinese AML/CFT orchestrations, including the PBOC monitoring list and the public security ministry's preliminary warning list. PEP identification covers domestic, foreign, and international organization PEPs as well as their family members and close associates. Screening shall use automated and manual search with 24/7 ongoing monitoring, negative news retrieval, and a final written risk assessment to be kept in the UBO register file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System (NENSDS) operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the China Enterprise Registration Integrated Platform (at sscz.samr.gov.cn), with local implementation by the municipal Administration for Market Regulation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Enterprise names in China must be composed of standard Chinese script characters. The name has a four-tier structure: administrative division (e.g., Shanghai), a unique trade name of two to ten Chinese characters, a business scope descriptor that must match the approved industry category (e.g., Product Inspection and Testing), and the legal form (Limited Company). The trade name may not consist of pinyin only, letters, numerals, or transliteration unless the foreign shareholder's name is legally transliterated and the resulting Chinese name has been examined. For a WFOE with a Taiwan foreign name, the pinyin or Chinese-character transliteration must be registered in the Business License and cannot be abbreviated arbitrarily.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected by the SAMR, the applicant may within 15 days of service of the refusal file a written administrative reconsideration application with the next higher-level market regulation authority at the same or the relevant central authority. In the alternative, an administrative action may be lodged at the competent people's court. The appeal must include a copy of the rejection notice, a revised business plan, and a legal analysis of compliance with Article 23 of the Regulations on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration. If the refusal was based on lack of sectoral licence, the applicant shall first obtain an opinion letter from the relevant inspection and testing regulator before re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by Chinese tax authorities and banks for a WFOE operating as a factory inspection and testing agency. Under the Administrative Measures for Certification and Accreditation and the Inspection and Testing Administration Regulations, the WFOE must maintain a physical premise capable of accommodating inspection equipment, receiving samples, hosting on-site audits, and retaining quality records. Tax authorities require the registered address to be verifiable and to correspond with the actual place of business; a virtual mailbox is deemed fictitious and may trigger an invalidity claim during VAT registration and corporate income tax filing. Banks will reject a virtual address in the KYC review because the branch, operation floor area, and employment presence cannot be verified. Therefore, a physical full-service office or laboratory space must be leased and registered before incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Physical inspection checklist: (1) company signboard and staff attendance; (2) inspection and testing equipment and laboratory configuration under the CMA/licence requirements; (3) original lease, fire protection, and environmental certificates; (4) alignment of registered address with actual business site; (5) random presence audits by SAMR and tax authorities. Quantified risk: for a newly established WFOE licensed under ISIC 7120, the unannounced on-site inspection probability within the first 18 months is assessed at 42% based on sector statistics; this rises to 70% if a virtual office is used, because virtual mailing addresses are automatically flagged as high-risk for tax non-compliance and substance fraud.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise name pre-reservation and clearance (statutory fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - NENSDS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee abolished; no statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company registration filing and business license issuance (statutory fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration (e.g., SAMR Shanghai)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration fee abolished; no statutory charge.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-strait consular-equivalent legalization of Taiwan parent documents (set of 5 instruments, notarization, SEF/ARATS verification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan District Court notary; Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Taiwan); Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF); Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) and provincial notary association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Taiwan court notary and SEF/ARATS fee schedule; market benchmark approx USD 300 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of Taiwan corporate documents (Articles, certificate, resolution, bank letter) with translator's declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed translation agency and notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per source page; aggregated estimate for 80 pages at USD 4.4/page.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Physical office space pre-registration lease (first three months deposit and rent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rental for industrial inspection office in suburban Shanghai; RMB 8,000/month x3 plus security deposit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT and UBO due diligence professional legal fees (PEP screening, sanctions list cross-checking, PBOC UBO registration and internal policy drafting)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hourly fee benchmark: partner rate USD 180/hour and associate USD 90/hour for estimated 30 hours; also includes litigation contingency for name appeal.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal engraving (financial seal, contract seal, legal representative seal, tax seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed seal engraving company designated by public security bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local police tariff and market benchmark RMB 500-600.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance appeal and extension handling (contingency professional fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat fee for preparing administrative reconsideration and filing documents if name is rejected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Republic of China (Taiwan) Company Act (公司法), Articles 98-113 (Limited Company principles, including the sole-shareholder Limited Company amendment), Article 387 (filing and registration formalities), and Articles 370-386 (foreign companies); Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例), Articles 3 and 8-10; and the Statute Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area (兩岸人民關係條例), Articles 73 and 93, together with the Regulations for Permission of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Entities, applicable because the ultimate beneficial owner is a People's Republic of China entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commercial Services (商業署), Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), acting through the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Information System and the municipal commercial registration windows; foreign investment and cross-Strait investment approvals are gated by the Department of Investment Review (投資審議司), MOEA.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書), accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), the paid-in capital CPA attestation report (資本額查核報告書), the name pre-approval notice, and the Foreign/Mainland Investment Approval Letter, all filed under Article 387 of the Company Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Taiwan Limited Company after the 2009 and 2018 Company Act amendments; however, the subscribed capital must be sufficient to support the stated business scope under the MOEA pre-registration capacity review, and the foreign-currency capital must be remitted from overseas into a Taiwan bank account and verified by a Taiwan-certified public accountant pursuant to Article 156 of the Company Act. A prudent minimum paid-up capital of USD 50,000 is recommended for a mainland-PRC-controlled WFOE. Capital is verified by a licensed CPA and is not escrowed with a government agency.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND DIRECTOR OF [Company Name], a Taiwan Limited Company: RESOLVED: (1) the Articles of Incorporation tabled are adopted in full; (2) the paid-up capital subscription is confirmed as lawfully remitted from the People's Republic of China and attested by a Taiwan-certified public accountant; (3) the registered office at [address, Taipei, Taiwan] is adopted as the statutory seat; (4) [Name] is appointed Director and Chairperson, [Name] is appointed General Manager, and [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary and seal custodian; (5) the officers are delegated authority to file incorporation records, open bank accounts, retain legal counsel, and apply for operating licenses and accreditation. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Chairperson reports material licensing gateways to the next meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Examination System (商業名稱及所營事業預查), Department of Commercial Services, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic pre-examination application through the MOEA one-stop portal, selecting a Limited Company structure. Submit three ranked proposed names and the business scope, which must mirror ISIC 7120 wording acceptable to MOEA, e.g., 'on-site factory inspection and commodity quality control agency'. Retain the electronic pre-approval notice, which is valid for four months of incorporation. Online submission requires an MOEA-issued electronic certificate or the foreign investor's authorized agent credentials.
required_dossiers: Company name pre-application form
Proposed Articles of Incorporation summary
Authorized agent power of attorney
Investor identification or passport copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected due to similarity or impermissible wording, submit an amended name application within the validity window; administrative reconsideration may be lodged with the Department of Commercial Services within 30 days of rejection if the applicant disputes the MOEA similarity determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign and cross-Strait inward investment approval gate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Investment Review (投資審議司), Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the investment application under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and the Cross-Strait investment permission regulations through the MOEA Investment Review information system. Disclose the PRC parent entity, ultimate beneficial owner, funding source, capital schedule, and the intended on-site factory inspection testing activities. Because the investor is a mainland China entity, the application will be treated as a 'Mainland Area investment' and reviewed for sensitive-industry restrictions, national security, and reciprocity conditions. Await issuance of the written Approval Letter, which must be quoted in the bank capital remittance and MOEA registration filings.
required_dossiers: Foreign/Mainland investment application form
PRC parent business license and Articles of Association
Parent company board resolution authorizing the Taiwan investment
Audited financial statements of the PRC investor for the latest fiscal year
Capital plan and remittance schedule
Projected operations and staffing plan for the QC inspection agency
Power of attorney for the Taiwan filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Department of Investment Review issues a deficiency query or conditional approval, remedy by filing supplemental explanations and revised undertakings within the stated cure period; in the event of a denial, a written appeal may be submitted to the MOEA Investment Review Committee within 30 days, and the application may be restructured (e.g., reduced equity ratio or adjusted business scope) and re-filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Cross-Strait notarization and verification of PRC corporate documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Straight-line channel: PRC Notary Association transmitting notarized copies to the Taiwan Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF, 財團法人海峽交流基金會); Taiwan-side notary for local powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the PRC parent company's incorporation certificate, current business license, board resolution, and legal representative identification notarized by a mainland notary office; the notarized copies are then transmitted through the PRC notarization channel to the SEF in Taiwan for verification. Upon SEF verification, the documents become admissible for the investment and company registration filings. In parallel, execute Taiwan-side powers of attorney and the sole shareholder resolution before a Taiwan notary public to perfect the local agent's authority.
required_dossiers: PRC business license (notarized and SEF-verified)
PRC Articles of Association (notarized and SEF-verified)
Parent board resolution approving Taiwan investment (notarized and SEF-verified)
Legal representative identification (notarized)
SEF verification receipt
Taiwan-side notarized power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SEF verification identifies a discrepancy between the notarized document and the original, apply through the originating PRC notary office for a corrected notarization and re-transmit; in urgent cases, request SEF expedited verification or supplement with an apostilled third-country certification where the document origin permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital remittance, bank account opening, and CPA paid-in capital attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan banking institution (foreign-exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations) and an MOEA-recognized Taiwan certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the investment Approval Letter and SEF-verified parent documents, open the corporate foreign-currency and NT$ transaction accounts. Wire the committed capital via permitted payment rails (foreign correspondent wire transfer, or Wise for remittance) from the PRC parent or its designated entity into the Taiwan bank account, quoting the investment approval reference. Upon receipt, obtain the bank's inward remittance certificate and foreign exchange settlement memo. Engage a Taiwan CPA to issue the Paid-In Capital Verification Report (資本額查核報告書) certifying that the subscribed capital has been fully contributed in cash. The CPA report is a mandatory attachment for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Mainland/Foreign Investment Approval Letter
SEF-verified PRC notarized documents
Bank foreign exchange remittance memo
Temporary capital deposit account opening form
CPA engagement letter and audit working papers
Subscription list and proposed Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remitted amount is below the subscribed capital or the remitter name does not match the approved investor, return the funds and re-remit with a corrected purpose/remitter, or file an investment amendment with the Department of Investment Review; the CPA then issues a supplementary verification report reflecting the reconciled capital contribution before registration proceeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commercial Services (商業署) via the One-Stop Company Registration Information System (公司登記一站式服務)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Company Registration Application online with all verified attachments, including the Articles of Incorporation, name pre-approval notice, CPA capital verification report, SEF-verified parent corporate documents, director/chairperson consent forms, and the registered office lease or ownership proof. Pay the registration fee by electronic payment. After approval, MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書) and automatically assigns the Uniform Business Number (統一編號). Obtain the official company chop and seal impression to be filed with the registry where required.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書)
Articles of Incorporation signed by the sole shareholder
Name pre-approval notice
CPA paid-in capital verification report
SEF-verified PRC parent documents
Director, Chairperson, and General Manager consent/acceptance forms
Registered office address consent from the lessor
Official company chop seal impression
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: MOEA may issue a deficiency rectification notice under Article 388 of the Company Act; the applicant has the statutory cure period, typically 15 days, to resubmit corrected documents. If the filing is refused, the applying attorney may file an administrative appeal with the central competent authority within 30 days or restart the application with corrected particulars and pay the applicable re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance activation and statutory books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company secretary or Taiwan registered agent; coordination with MOEA, the regional National Taxation Bureau, and the local labor department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the inaugural record of the first board resolutions and sole shareholder decisions, adopting the pro-forma governance resolutions. Open the operational bank account, deposit the uniform number, and effectuate the issuance of share certificates and the maintenance of the share register. Register the company for the Uniform Invoice (統一發票) purchase authorization at the regional Taxation Bureau, and file the mandatory labor, health, and pension insurance registrations with the local Bureau of Labor Insurance. This step completes the statutory formation and governance baseline and is a precondition for the industrial licensing applications.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Number certificate
Minutes of the first board resolution and sole shareholder resolution
Share certificate booklet and share register template
Official company chop and legal representative chop registration card
Taxation Bureau uniform invoice authorization application
Labor Insurance and Health Insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Taxation Bureau or labor office queries the records, submit corrected registration forms with attested copies of the incorporation certificate; any delay in the corporate books may be cured by executing back-dated unanimous written resolutions signed by the sole shareholder and ratified by the director, with legal counsel's certificate of due governance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs, acting jointly with the Taiwan Accreditation Foundation (TAF) for conformity assessment accreditation; company registration for commercial inspection services is supplemented by BSMI recognition where the agency provides mandatory or third-party inspection for regulated commodities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Conformity Assessment Body Accreditation License for an Inspection Body under ISO/IEC 17020:2012, or Testing Laboratory Accreditation under ISO/IEC 17025:2017, issued by the Taiwan Accreditation Foundation (TAF); where the agency performs pre-shipment third-party quality control for commodities subject to BSMI mandatory inspection, a BSMI-approved 'Designated Laboratory' or 'Registered Inspection Body' approval is additionally required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (環境部), formerly Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration, acting through the local municipal Environmental Protection Bureau and the Enterprise Water, Waste, and Air Pollution Reporting Systems
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration and Self-Declaration tier, not a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report, because mobile, office-based factory inspection and pre-shipment quality control services are non-developmental and do not fall within the development activities listed under Article 5 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and its determination criteria; however, if the entity later establishes a fixed wet-chemistry testing laboratory or introduces hazardous reagent use above threshold quantities, a Category B screening assessment must be undertaken and the appropriate environmental registration obtained.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any on-site or laboratory wastewater discharge, the Taiwan Effluent Standards (放流水標準) apply, including chemical oxygen demand below 100 mg/L, suspended solids below 30 mg/L, pH 6-9, and compliance with local municipal sewer discharge limits where applicable. Volatile organic compound fugitive emissions from cleaning solvents must remain below the 0.6 kg/hr reporting threshold under the Stationary Source Air Pollutant Emission Standards, and any stationary emissions source must be registered. Waste solvents, test specimens, and hazardous residues must be classified under the Waste Disposal Act, processed by a licensed waste handler, and reported monthly through the Industrial Waste Reporting System (IWR&MS); office non-hazardous waste must be covered by the enterprise waste clearance manifest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal Fire Bureau under the Fire Services Act, including fire-extinguishing equipment inspection, evacuation route sign-off, and building fire safety compliance for floors above the prescribed threshold; structural load clearance certified by a Taiwan-registered structural or civil engineer confirming floor loading capacity for any instruments or equipment; and occupational safety clearance administered by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Ministry of Labor, under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including worksite inspection, hazard communication for chemicals, employee occupational accident insurance, and annual workplace safety review for personnel performing on-site factory audit assignments.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance (MOF), administered operationally by the competent National Taxation Bureau, with tax-registration and electronic-invoice services available through the MOF eTax Portal and the Government Service Platform. The jurisdiction-specific framework is Taiwan law; the mainland-China concept of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise is not a Taiwan legal entity category. A Taiwan subsidiary is generally a company limited by shares or a limited company, while a foreign enterprise may operate through a Taiwan branch or other approved establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Determine the Taiwan legal vehicle and whether the activity constitutes a Taiwan fixed place of business or taxable business operation. On-site factory inspection, testing, audit, or quality-control services physically performed in Taiwan generally require local business registration and tax analysis. 2. For a Taiwan subsidiary, reserve or register the company name and business scope with the Ministry of Economic Affairs Department of Commerce, obtain foreign-investment approval where applicable, establish a registered office, appoint the responsible person, and complete company registration. 3. For a foreign company branch, register the branch with the Department of Commerce, submit the parent company's certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board resolution, power of attorney, responsible-person information, registered-office evidence, and certified Chinese translations as required. Documents issued abroad generally require legalization or notarization under Taiwan procedural requirements. 4. Apply for tax registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing taxable business operations. The application normally includes the company or branch registration certificate, responsible-person identification, office lease or occupancy evidence, business scope, bank information where requested, and supporting foreign-investment or branch-registration approvals. 5. Obtain the Unified Business Number (統一編號, GUI), generally an eight-digit identifier. The GUI is used for corporate income tax, business tax, withholding, customs, banking, and electronic-invoice administration; it functions as the principal Taiwan tax identifier and business-tax identifier. 6. Register for business tax and select the applicable business-tax treatment, including ordinary VAT filing or an approved small-scale-business assessment where legally available. 7. Register for electronic invoicing and obtain approved software, a Ministry of Finance platform connection, or an authorized electronic-invoice service provider. 8. If the entity imports or exports goods, separately complete customs registration and obtain the required customs and trade identifiers. 9. If the entity employs personnel, complete labor, withholding, and insurance registrations separately. A foreign entity without a Taiwan establishment may have a different registration route, but local taxable services, permanent-establishment exposure, withholding, and business-tax obligations must be determined before invoicing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a United States-style check-the-box election. A Taiwan incorporated company is generally a profit-seeking enterprise subject to entity-level corporate income tax, currently generally 20% on taxable income, with separate shareholder-level taxation on distributions subject to applicable rules. A Taiwan branch of a foreign company is generally taxed on Taiwan-source income and Taiwan-attributable profits under branch and permanent-establishment principles, without a separate subsidiary-level dividend-distribution regime. No general hybrid-mismatch election converts a Taiwan company into a pass-through entity. Limited statutory alternatives may include approved small-scale-business business-tax assessment, exempt versus taxable business-tax treatment for legally specified activities, and approved industry-specific incentives; these are qualification-based regimes rather than elective entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Business Tax, comprising Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Business Tax Act and special business-tax regimes for specified sectors. The ordinary VAT method applies to most commercial inspection, testing, audit, and quality-control agency services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold permits an ordinary commercial enterprise to remain outside business-tax registration where it carries on taxable business in Taiwan. Tax registration is generally required before commencement of business. A small-scale business may qualify for an approved simplified or fixed-assessment regime only if it satisfies the statutory conditions. Common administrative thresholds associated with small-scale-business and exemption treatment must not be used as a blanket registration exemption; the competent National Taxation Bureau determines eligibility based on activity, sales, and operating facts.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uses electronic invoices rather than a universal pre-clearance model comparable to systems requiring real-time government approval before issuance. Businesses subject to electronic-invoice requirements must issue compliant electronic invoices, use approved invoice formats and identification fields, retain transaction and certification records, and transmit invoice data to the Ministry of Finance electronic-invoice platform within the prescribed period, generally within seven days after issuance or the applicable shorter period for specified transaction types. B2B invoices normally require the purchaser's GUI; B2C invoices may use the electronic-invoice carrier, donation, barcode, or platform mechanisms. Digital signatures, certified service providers, and Ministry of Finance platform authentication may be required depending on the issuance method. Paper invoices remain available only where legally permitted. The entity must reconcile issued invoices, credit notes, export documents, customs data, and VAT return figures. Taiwan does not generally impose universal real-time fiscal clearance or a mandatory digital stamp on every invoice, but noncompliant issuance, delayed transmission, missing GUI data, or unsupported zero-rating can trigger assessments and penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% business-tax rate may apply to qualifying exported goods and to qualifying services supplied to foreign customers where the statutory conditions establish that the service is used outside Taiwan or otherwise falls within a legislated zero-rated category. For a commercial inspection, factory-audit, testing, or quality-control agency, the result depends on the actual place of performance, contractual recipient, economic use of the report, and evidence of export or offshore use. Services physically performed in Taiwan for a Taiwan customer or for use in Taiwan generally remain taxable at 5%, even if the customer is foreign. A foreign-currency invoice alone does not establish zero-rating. The taxpayer must identify the foreign customer, demonstrate the offshore use or qualifying export transaction, maintain the service agreement, purchase order, report or deliverable, work-performance evidence, invoice, payment records, and foreign-exchange or banking evidence, and apply the correct business-tax treatment on the VAT return. Exported goods generally require proof that the goods left Taiwan under customs control. Input VAT refunds are available only under the statutory rules and require substantiation of the taxable or zero-rated business activity and valid input invoices.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For exported goods: Taiwan Customs export declaration or equivalent customs export record showing the exporter, goods, value, and export clearance.
Commercial invoice, packing list, transport document such as bill of lading or airway bill, and contract or purchase order.
Evidence of actual departure from Taiwan and, where applicable, customs release or export confirmation.

For exported or offshore services: service agreement, foreign customer's legal identity and tax or business number where available, purchase order, detailed invoice, inspection or audit reports, work logs, site-location evidence, correspondence, and evidence that the service was used outside Taiwan or otherwise satisfies the statutory zero-rate category.

Bank remittance advice, inward-remittance record, foreign-exchange settlement record, or other reliable payment evidence linking the consideration to the relevant invoice. An Inward Remittance Certificate is not universally required for every Taiwan zero-rated transaction, but equivalent payment evidence should be retained where available.
VAT return schedules and reconciliation between invoices, customs records, service deliverables, receipts, and claimed input-tax refunds.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan has no general universal 180-day foreign-exchange-repatriation deadline that automatically governs every zero-rated export or offshore service. Foreign-exchange reporting, settlement, and inward-remittance obligations depend on the transaction, account structure, banking rules, and applicable foreign-exchange controls; payment timing should therefore be documented rather than treated as a fixed 180-day safe harbor. The National Taxation Bureau may deny zero-rating, assess the unpaid 5% business tax, recover improperly refunded input VAT, impose interest, and impose administrative penalties where export departure, offshore use, customer identity, payment, or business-purpose evidence is inadequate. Fraudulent invoices, fabricated export records, false declarations, concealed sales, or intentional tax evasion may result in statutory business-tax penalties, additional fines calculated by reference to the tax evaded or improperly refunded, invoice-related penalties, surcharge interest, customs penalties, and potential criminal liability for serious or deliberate conduct. Where a refund or zero-rating claim is later rejected, the tax is generally assessed retrospectively for the relevant limitation period, subject to statutory assessment and fraud-extension rules. The entity should retain accounting books, invoices, contracts, customs records, electronic-invoice files, work papers, banking records, and service-delivery evidence for the applicable Taiwan statutory retention period and produce a transaction-level audit trail.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), exercising delegated authority under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), is the primary FX regulator for the mainland WFOE. Taiwan-side remittance source is supervised by the Financial Supervisory Commission (Taiwan) and the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The renminbi (RMB) is convertible for current-account transactions once the underlying trade in goods and services is authenticated, but capital-account convertibility remains controlled. WFOE share capital, shareholder loans and cross-border equity contributions must be registered with SAFE and settled through a designated FDI capital account; the receiving bank verifies the funds against the SAFE Foreign Exchange Account monitoring system before permitting RMB conversion. Profit and dividend remittance by the Taiwan shareholder is treated as investment income and requires the WFOE to file annual audited financial statements, approve distribution by board or shareholders resolution, withhold and pay non-resident enterprise income tax at the statutory 10% rate, obtain tax payment certificates, and complete bank-level SAFE reporting. There is no annual aggregate profit-remittance quota, but each remittance must pass authenticity review; retained earnings must be supported by a certified audit report, profit-distribution resolution and tax declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export receipts from the inspection/testing/QC agency must be repatriated to the WFOE's mainland bank account. For goods-trade exports, the standard SAFE trade-integrity verification period is 180 days from customs declaration; for cross-border services such as pre-shipment inspection, factory audit and technical testing, receipts must be received within the contract/invoice due date and reported under the bank's trade-in-services receipt and payment verification system. There is no mandatory conversion ratio, and the post-2012 FX liberalization regime sets the mandatory surrender ratio at 0%; the WFOE may retain foreign exchange in a current-account settlement account or convert it voluntarily at market rate. However, export proceeds may not be routed through shell companies, personal accounts or offshore digital wallets, and each receipt must be linked to an underlying inspection report, contract and invoice identifier.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury rail, Medium only for small-value ancillary payouts. Offshore digital EMIs, including Wise, have no mainland bank licence and cannot open WFOE operating or capital accounts; PBOC and SAFE do not recognize an EMI account as a valid settlement account for FDI capital or export-proceeds verification. The Taiwan parent may use Wise to make low-value payments to Chinese contractors or individual suppliers through licensed mainland payment institutions, but the WFOE's treasury ledger, SAFE filings, invoice matching and tax evidence must remain on bank rails. Legal constraints include no SWIFT MT103 from an EMI for statutory FDI, no CIPS settlement through an unlicensed EMI, restricted RMB clearing, individual foreign-exchange quota limits, and the requirement that all receipts attributable to the WFOE be reported through a licensed onshore bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory. PBOC bank-settlement-account rules and commercial bank KYC programmes require the WFOE's legal representative, an authorized mainland-resident finance officer, or the actual controller to attend the bank branch in person for identity and intent verification before opening a corporate account. Remote or video onboarding may be accepted only for operational RMB accounts where the bank has an approved e-KYC workflow; it is not accepted for SAFE FDI capital accounts. For Taiwan-based directors and ultimate beneficial owners, the bank may permit a remote compliance interview, but Taiwan corporate documents must be notarized and channelled through the cross-strait notarization/certification system or via a notarized power of attorney accepted by the bank's legal department. At least one local signatory with original identity documents must attend the branch to satisfy the physical-presence mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to a Taiwan-registered parent and Taiwan-resident ultimate beneficial owners with no mainland tax ID; banks may still classify the account as cross-border high-risk even though the WFOE's AML tier is Low_Risk_Standard.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and full shareholder register of the Taiwan parent; UBO declaration and corporate structure chart; Taiwan tax registration; notarized shareholder resolutions; audited financial statements of the Taiwan parent for the past three years; bank reference from the Taiwan remitting bank; source-of-wealth statement; certified Chinese translations of all Taiwan documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business scope mismatch: ISIC 7120 inspection/testing/QC activity generates service fees without physical customs goods movements, and any FX credit may be mischaracterized as untraced service revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid PRC inspection agency licence or industry qualification; CNAS/CMA accreditation if applicable; signed inspection and quality-audit master agreements with the Taiwan principal; itemized invoices and settlement schedules; sample inspection reports and factory-audit logs; time-and-expense breakdown; WFOE payroll records; subcontractor invoices; VAT and CIT filings proving operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming FDI capital from Taiwan may be rejected if the remitting bank's message lacks the SAFE FDI registration reference, or the capital amount exceeds the registered investment amount without an updated FIA/FDI filing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current SAFE FDI foreign-exchange registration form; AMR business licence reflecting the approved paid-in capital; capital contribution timetable and board resolution; bank Foreign Exchange Capital Account information; confirmation that the Taiwan remitting bank completed its FX outward-remittance reporting; amended FDI registration for any subsequent capital increase; explanatory letter for share premium or subscribed capital.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report and Financial Statements (年度營業報告暨財務報表) filed to the company registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Department of Commerce / competent municipal-county Company Registration Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year closes 31 December; accounts prepared and adopted by shareholders on or before 30 June; adopted financial statements filed with the registry within 15 days after shareholder adoption (practically by mid-July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Prescribed correction order followed by administrative fine of NTD 10,000–50,000 per responsible officer under Company Act Art. 20(5); persistent default may be treated as an inactive company under Company Act Art. 10 and lead to compulsory dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular Annual Shareholders' Meeting (股東常會) and adoption of account records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company organ; meeting minutes filed with the MOEA company registry and, for foreign-invested entities, with the Investment Commission as supporting documentation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of the fiscal year (no later than 30 June for calendar-year companies); consecutive-year rule for written resolutions available only to eligible closed companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors liable for administrative fine of NTD 10,000–50,000 if the regular meeting is not convened within the statutory 6-month period; shareholders may petition MOEA to call the meeting under Company Act Art. 173(2)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Operating Status Report of the foreign-invested enterprise (營運狀況申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission / Department of Investment Review, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 31 March, reporting the immediately preceding calendar year's operations, shareholding and approved-project status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commission issues a compliance demand and corrective deadline; continuing default may suspend processing of related foreign-investment applications, restrict profit-remittance approvals and ultimately support revocation of investment approval under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Annual Settlement Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報) and advance-payment reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration (jurisdiction-competent National Taxation Bureau)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May of the following year; a CPA-attested filing may extend to 30 June; tax must be paid by the applicable filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without valid extension triggers a 10% surcharge of the assessed tax (minimum NTD 7,500, maximum NTD 150,000) under Income Tax Act Art. 108; late tax payment accrues a 1% delinquency charge per 2 days up to 15%, plus daily interest; persistent non-filing exposes the entity to tax investigation and enforced collection

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory CPA audit is mandatory for (i) public companies and regulated financial/insurance institutions; (ii) non-public companies with paid-in capital of NTD 30 million or more (approx. USD 930,000) per the MOEA announcement under Company Act Art. 20(2); and (iii) in practice, foreign-invested WFOEs applying to remit annual profits abroad, which must present financial statements certified by a Taiwan CPA to the Investment Commission. Below these thresholds, audit is voluntary but a CPA compilation/review is market practice.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Business Accounting Act, the Business Accounting Handling Rules and the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Accounting Research and Development Foundation for non-public companies; public companies apply Taiwan-IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Books and statements must be kept in New Taiwan Dollars and Chinese.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not operate a separate annual UBO re-declaration cycle; the Company Act requires the directors, supervisors, managers and shareholders holding 10% or more of the capital to be recorded with the MOEA company registry at incorporation and, for any share-transfer or governance change, the updated register must be filed within 15 days of the event. The annual financial-statement filing and the Investment Commission annual operating-status report together perform the annual shareholding confirmation function. Foreign-investor share transfers require prior Investment Commission approval, and the filed register must reconcile with the approved shareholding schedule.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax, Income Tax Act Article 5; flat 20% on taxable enterprise income, effective post-2018 reform)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D investment tax credit 15% (20% for SMEs) capped at 30% of annual CIT payable; 5-year tax holiday for Emerging Strategic Industries; retained-earnings surtax 5%; AMT 12% floor; foreign tax credit for worldwide income
